items.title: COR-CFN-26-010, Development Charges Update
notes:
W. Steffler introduced the report, which provides an update on changes to the development charges framework. 

Maria Laguna, Manager, Infrastructure Financing, provided a presentation and an overview of the Provincial and Regional legislative changes. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda.

In response to questions from Committee, M. Laguna confirmed that staff are looking into if the new provincial program would be worth applying for, this will depend on the project.

Staff also confirmed that the Region is on the lower end of development charges compared to their comparator municipalities. Staff also confirmed that they will be working with the treasurers of the area municipalities ahead of the provincial deadline later in June.

Staff confirmed that under the new program municipalities would be required to contribute at least 10% towards a project.

In response to further questions, staff explained that analysis on this program is ongoing and will take time to complete, but that initial funding will most likely be achieved through issuing debt.

items.title: COR-CFN-26-008, 2027 Plan and Budget Approach and Timeline
notes:
Darshpreet Bhatti, Chief Administrative Officer, provided an introduction to the report. 

A presentation was provided by D. Bhatti, Connie MacDonald, Commissioner, Resident Experience, Strategy and Communications, and W. Steffler, a copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda.

In response to questions from Committee, staff explained that while they can work with WRPS to aim for a certain percentage increase in their budget in 2027, they cannot direct WRPS to present a specific percentage.

Committee expressed interest in staff exploring a rotational budget review cycle. This would allow for a deeper examination into each department's budget once every four years. Staff confirmed they would look further into this review cycle and report back.

Committee also expressed interest in staff preparing multiple proposed budget scenarios; including returning with a proposal that increases the tax levy by the rate of inflation only, and one proposal that increases by inflation plus one percent.

Staff also confirmed that the current target percentage for the upcoming budget is not a growth scenario; but rather keeping all existing services and service levels in place, anything less will likely mean a reduction in services.

Committee inquired into how much of the current strategic plan has been completed so far. C. MacDonald shared that several parts of the plan were complete but would follow up with further details.

In response to questions from Committee, W. Steffler explained that the current water user rates are based on what was presented in the 2026 budget, an update on this is currently planned to return to Council in July.

Committee expressed interest in staff looking further into ability of citizens to pay taxes and how a tax increase would impact different groups, as well as cost of living impacts. Committee also expressed interest in the idea of having an auditor general department for the Region to look at budget efficiencies to report directly to Council and the public.  

Committee also directed staff to return with the data on WRPS' full complement of hires and the percentage increase over the past four years.

motions.item_title: COR-CFN-26-009, Q1 2026 Plan and Financial Update
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2026 first quarter update as set out in report COR-CFN-26-009 dated June 2, 2026: Receive the 2026 First Quarter Update that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Growing with Care 2023-2027 Strategic Plan; and Amend the 2026 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix B.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2026 first quarter update as set out in report COR-CFN-26-009 dated June 2, 2026:  

  1. Receive the 2026 First Quarter Update that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Growing with Care 2023-2027 Strategic Plan; and 
  2. Amend the 2026 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix B.

motions.text: Whereas Under the ESA, 2000, an employee is currently entitled to unpaid Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, provided they have at least two (2) months of continuous employment and Whereas if the employee is taking Reservist Leave because they are deployed to a Canadian Forces operation inside Canada related to handling an emergency or its aftermath, there is no minimum employment requirement and Whereas recent amendments via the Working for Workers Act, 2023, have expanded this leave to also include recovery from deployment-related injuries or illnesses and Whereas the current ESA leave type creates a "break in service" in OMERS, which can potentially reduce an employee’s credited service and future retirement benefits and Whereas, currently, the Region has not elected to share the cost of contributions, meaning that the employee is responsible for both their portion and the employer's portion, known as "double contributions" and Whereas OMERS regulations permit the purchase of service for certain leaves of absence, including those mandated by statute, to restore full credited service. For Reservist Leave, the employee may elect to buy back the period by contributing their share of premiums, with the employer matching its portion. This process requires explicit employer approval and, for municipal entities, formal authorization via a bylaw to ensure compliance with the Municipal Act, 2001, and to allocate public funds appropriately and Whereas the proposed bylaw will honour the employee's service to both the municipality and the nation, while upholding OMERS eligibility rules and Whereas the there are minimal financial implications associated with approving the OMERS Reservist Leave By-law and where an employee elects to take a Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, the Region as the employer will make an equal OMERS contribution in accordance with subsection 12(3) of the Primary Plan, funded from within the existing divisional operating budget, Now therefore be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo adopt the OMERS Region of Waterloo Reservist Bylaw to authorize the Region to match OMERS contributions for employees purchasing OMERS broken service resulting from an approved Reservist Leave, in accordance with the Employment Standards Act (ESA), 2000.
motions.text_html:
Whereas Under the ESA, 2000, an employee is currently entitled to unpaid Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, provided they have at least two (2) months of continuous employment and
Whereas if the employee is taking Reservist Leave because they are deployed to a Canadian Forces operation inside Canada related to handling an emergency or its aftermath, there is no minimum employment requirement and 
Whereas recent amendments via the Working for Workers Act, 2023, have expanded this leave to also include recovery from deployment-related injuries or illnesses and
Whereas the current ESA leave type creates a "break in service" in OMERS, which can potentially reduce an employee’s credited service and future retirement benefits and
Whereas, currently, the Region has not elected to share the cost of contributions, meaning that the employee is responsible for both their portion and the employer's portion, known as "double contributions" and 
Whereas OMERS regulations permit the purchase of service for certain leaves of absence, including those mandated by statute, to restore full credited service. For Reservist Leave, the employee may elect to buy back the period by contributing their share of premiums, with the employer matching its portion. This process requires explicit employer approval and, for municipal entities, formal authorization via a bylaw to ensure compliance with the Municipal Act, 2001, and to allocate public funds appropriately and 
Whereas the proposed bylaw will honour the employee's service to both the municipality and the nation, while upholding OMERS eligibility rules and 
Whereas the there are minimal financial implications associated with approving the OMERS Reservist Leave By-law and where an employee elects to take a Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, the Region as the employer will make an equal OMERS contribution in accordance with subsection 12(3) of the Primary Plan, funded from within the existing divisional operating budget, 
Now therefore be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo adopt the OMERS Region of Waterloo Reservist Bylaw to authorize the Region to match OMERS contributions for employees purchasing OMERS broken service resulting from an approved Reservist Leave, in accordance with the Employment Standards Act (ESA), 2000.
